bit string types.name: opcode
bit string types.description: rrq and wrq packets (opcodes 1 and 2 respectively) have the format shown in figure 5-1.

bit string types.name: filename
bit string types.description: the file name is a sequence of bytes in netascii terminated by a zero byte.

bit string types.name: mode
bit string types.description: the mode field contains the string "netascii", "octet", or "mail" (or any combination of upper and lower case, such as "netascii", netascii", etc.) in netascii indicating the three modes defined in the protocol.

bit string types.name: opcode
bit string types.description: data packets (opcode = 3) have a block number and data field.

bit string types.name: block number
bit string types.description: the block numbers on data packets begin with one and increase by one for each new block of data.

bit string types.name: data
bit string types.description: the data field is from zero to 512 bytes long. if it is 512 bytes long, the block is not the last block of data; if it is from zero to 511 bytes long, it signals the end of the transfer.

bit string types.name: opcode
bit string types.description: figure 5-3 depicts an ack packet; the opcode is 4.

bit string types.name: block number
bit string types.description: the block number in an ack echoes the block number of the data packet being acknowledged. a wrq is acknowledged with an ack packet having a block number of zero.

bit string types.name: opcode
bit string types.description: an error packet (opcode 5) takes the form depicted in figure 5-4.

bit string types.name: error code
bit string types.description: the error code is an integer indicating the nature of the error. a table of values and meanings is given in the appendix.

bit string types.name: err msg
bit string types.description: the error message is intended for human consumption, and should be in netascii. like all other strings, it is terminated with a zero byte.
